records.title: Mosaic
records.text: True to its name, Mosaic brings together several concepts—including content, design and technical infrastructure—to deliver a unified website experience that is truly greater than the sum of its individual parts. With Mosaic, you can: Don't move your content where it does not belong. Compose content from remote data sources which are pulled at runtime by our content aggregator. Visualize your content with your own theme, layouts and components or use the Mosaic Design language. Extend the existing code and add your own content source types through our simple plugin architecture. Publish your content through Server Side Rendering (SSR) or generate a snapshot of your content and serve it as a Statically Generated Site (SGS). Creating a website has never been so easy!

records.title: Aliases
records.text: Aliases are virtual 'symlinks' of pages, allowing one page to take on one or more other routes. This is not the same as copying the page, it is a primitive filesystem link which is resolved by Mosaic.

records.title: Aliases
records.text: Aliases are great for linking to an old route if you've moved a page to a new place. They can also be used to create short hand links to pages or to 'clone' a copy of a page into another section of the site where it may be relevant.

records.title: Fragments
records.text: Fragments, also known as content fragments, are powerful tools that allow you to incorporate content from other pages into your documentation. By creating an MDX file and using the generic directives syntax :fragment{src="path-to-fragment"} , you can easily render the fragment in another file, providing modularity and reusability to your content.

records.title: Fragments
records.text: Fragments offer various use cases, such as: Consistent Content : Use fragments to maintain consistent content across multiple pages. For instance, if you have a table or a tile that appears on multiple pages, you can create a fragment for it and include it in all relevant files. This ensures that any updates made to the fragment automatically reflect across the entire documentation. Reusable Components : Fragments enable the creation of reusable components or sections. You can define a complex or commonly used section once and then include it in multiple pages as needed. This approach saves time and effort, as you only need to update the fragment file to propagate changes throughout your documentation. Modular Documentation : With fragments, you can break down your documentation into smaller, manageable pieces. Each fragment represents a specific topic or section, allowing you to organize and structure your content more efficiently. This modular approach simplifies maintenance and makes it easier to navigate and update your documentation.

records.title: Refs
records.text: Refs are a very powerful feature of Mosaic documents that use JSON References to reference a property from the page frontmatter or frontmatter of other pages. The key concept is that of a JSON pointer which takes the form A # B where: A is the relative path from the current schema to a target schema. If A is empty, the reference is to a type or property in the same schema, an in-schema reference. Otherwise, the reference is to a different schema, a cross-schema reference. B is the complete path from the root of the schema to a type or property in the schema. If # in not included or B is empty, the reference is to an entire schema. To translate this for our purposes: A is the relative path to a file in the filesystem. B is the path to a property in the frontmatter of the file. It's probably better explained with examples...

records.title: Sidebar Configuration
records.text: Sidebar data is generated by the Sidebar Plugin , which uses page priorities and configured sort fields to order pages.

records.title: Sidebar Configuration
records.text: A page can add a sidebar property to its frontmatter to change the ordering of a sidebar and what title is used for a page in the sidebar. To rearrange pages in the sidebar or to apply a different label to a page you can specify the following in the page frontmatter:

records.title: Sidebar Configuration
records.text: A sidebar group when expanded will reveal the pages contained within the group. Each group has a default page, index.mdx , which is the default for the group and any breadcrumb link. The index.mdx can define a groupLabel which defines the name of the sidebar group. If no groupLabel is defined, sidebar group labels will be defined by either label or title . To specify the label of the default page, refer to [Sidebar label](./Sidebar label)

records.title: Sidebar Configuration
records.text: By default the title of a page is used in the sidebar as the label but this can be changed to another label using page frontmatter.

records.title: Sidebar Configuration
records.text: Sidebar priority is a number used to sort the sidebar. Higher the priority pages appear first in the sidebar ordering.

records.title: Sidebar Configuration
records.text: This hides the page from the sidebar and previous/next navigation. It does not hide child pages. An excluded index.mdx , including a namespace landing page, still defines the group's label, priority, and sort configuration. Groups with no visible descendants are omitted.

records.title: Sidebar Configuration
records.text: Sidebar sort configuration allows the sidebar to be sorted using a more sophisticated approach and only needs to be applied to the index page of the directory you want to sort. Priority takes precedence over sort configuration so it can be used to override the sort configuration if required. You must add the sidebar sort configuration to the sharedConfig.sidebar.sort property of an index page e.g., The properties of the sort configuration are described in the table below: | Property | Description | Required | | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | | field | the path, separated by / , used to find the value in page frontmatter you wish to sort by | Yes | | dataType | is the type of the value. Can be a string or number or date . | Yes | | arrange | asc or desc order | yes |

records.title: Sidebar Configuration
records.text: Let's say you have a Newsletters directory and each page in the directory represents a newsletter. You wish to sort the newsletter sidebar by publication date in descending order (newest first). One way to do this is to edit each page and add a priority which is manually incremented every time a news newsletter is added. Alternatively you can add the following sort configuration to the newsletters index page: This will use the data.publicationDate property in each newsletter to sort the newsletters in the sidebar. The publication date is converted to a date by the Sidebar Plugin to ensure accurate ordering. There is now no need to increment a priority when a new newsletter is added. records.title: Tags
records.text: Tags are very similar to Refs with one very important distinction: Tags work across multiple sources . In Mosaic, each source has it's own filesystem which are then merged together to form a union of all source filesystems. It is in this union filesystem that tags are applied and not to the individual source filesystem that the tag was defined on. Tags are slower to apply than refs. Multiple sources need to run and update before tagged data will be resolved. If possible, stick to refs and only use tags when dealing with multiple sources.

records.title: Tags
records.text: To tag a page, add a tags property to the page frontmatter. For example, the Product A page is tagged with "in-stock": tags is always an array

records.title: Tags
records.text: To subscribe to a tag, use the $tag property. For example, the Products page has subscribed to the data property of pages tagged with in-stock . A $tag can provide a path to a specific piece of metadata on tagged pages, just like a ref.

records.title: UI Components
records.text: Use components that render inline HTML inside a paragraph. For example, Tag accepts either a label or children: An explicit label takes precedence over children, including label="" . Typography components such as Subtitle5 render a paragraph by default. Use component="span" when placing one inside a sentence:

records.title: UI Components
records.text: Link in the default MDX registry is Mosaic's Link , whose props differ from Salt's Link . Use endIcon="none" to hide its trailing icon; Salt's IconComponent prop is not supported. Standard aria-* and data-* attributes can still be passed through. Headings can contain normal Markdown links. The separate copy control beside a heading copies its permalink without intercepting links in the heading text.

records.title: UI Components
headings: Values that differ between server and browser
records.text: The initial browser render must match the HTML rendered by the server. Format dates with an explicit locale and time zone when displaying them in MDX, rather than relying on each machine's defaults: Keep browser-dependent values inside components that apply them after hydration. A host can opt into an MDX Suspense boundary for recovery and suspending content, but this does not make invalid HTML or inconsistent initial values correct.

records.title: UI Components
records.text: Cards and its Tiles alias accept Salt GridLayout props. For example, columns={{ xs: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }} selects one, two, or three columns using CSS before hydration. The breakpoint sizes come from the surrounding Salt provider, including custom breakpoints . Numeric columns and the existing grid spacing props continue to work. This behavior applies to Mosaic's wrappers; a host's direct use of Salt GridLayout keeps Salt's own responsive behavior.

records.title: Create a Site
records.text: In this guide you will learn how to generate and serve a Mosaic site.

records.title: Create a Site
records.text: To begin setting up a Mosaic site, you need to have the following software installed: Yarn v4.10.3 or higher Node.js v24 or higher

records.title: Create a Site
headings: Step 1: Set Up a Mosaic Site
records.text: Export the site package from this repository into your project. It is a standard Next.js App Router app that loads the packages created by this repo, with an additional mosaic.config.mjs file to configure sources and other settings. Yarn's pack command converts the template's workspace: dependencies to published version ranges, so the exported site can install outside the monorepo. Steps: Export and install the template: Configure the contents of the exported site as needed. Update mosaic.config.mjs to specify your content sources and other options. Replace the reference paths to this monorepo's documentation folders with paths to your own content. A local source is used to serve pages from the local file-system, which can be a clone of a remote repo. A remote source is used to pull content from a remote Git repository. Note: App Router layout. The site uses Next.js App Router ( src/app/ ), not the legacy Pages Router ( src/pages/ ). Key files you'll touch when customising: src/app/layout.tsx — root layout, global CSS and fonts. src/app/providers.tsx — client-side provider stack (optional authentication, theme, store, layout). src/app/[namespace]/[...route]/page.tsx — the catch-all RSC route that loads content with the @jpmorganchase/mosaic-site-middleware loaders and renders MDX. src/app/[namespace]/[...route]/MdxComponents.ts — registry for MDX-visible components (replaces the old _app.tsx component merge). src/auth.ts — Auth.js v5 wiring ( handlers , auth , signIn , signOut ). With auth enabled, providers.tsx mounts <SessionProvider> and <NextAuthAdapter> without a server-resolved session. The browser fetches the session after the page loads. With auth disabled, neither auth provider is mounted and no session request is made. Keep that pattern when you copy the directory; the site's README.md lists the other patterns to preserve. Upgrading a site built on the Pages Router? See Migrate to the App Router . Next, navigate to your new site directory:

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: The reference Mosaic site ( packages/site ) has moved from the Next.js Pages Router to the App Router. A follow-up release secured the editor and the content server, changed some deployment defaults, and removed snapshot-s3 mode and mosaic upload . This guide covers everything you need to change if your site was copied from the old Pages Router site, or if you run the Mosaic CLI ( mosaic serve , mosaic build or mosaic upload ). Your site uses the old layout if it has src/pages/_app.tsx and src/pages/[...route].tsx . Content authors don't need to change anything. Pages are still MDX with the same frontmatter, and references such as {meta.title} still work.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: Start from a fresh export of the current packages/site , following Create a Site , and move your customisations into it, rather than converting your old files in place. The export converts workspace dependencies to published version ranges. Almost every file in the site has changed, and the new files contain fixes you'd otherwise have to rediscover. The site's README.md lists the patterns you must keep under "Critical patterns to preserve when copying". Keep your mosaic.config.mjs , your content, your CSS and your own components. Then work through the sections below.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: Node.js 24 or later. The reference Docker images use Node.js 24. Next.js 16.4.2 or later, and React 19. Earlier Next.js 16 releases (and 15.x before 15.5.28) are affected by remote code execution and denial of service advisories ( GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 , GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36 , GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw , GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r ). Upgrade every @jpmorganchase/mosaic-* package to the same version. mosaic-site-middleware , mosaic-site-components and mosaic-layouts have breaking changes, so don't mix old and new versions. For hosts using Auth.js, install next-auth v5 ( next-auth@^5.0.0-beta ) in place of v4 and add the Mosaic adapter described below. Hosts without authentication do not need this package. mosaic-site-middleware , mosaic-site-components and mosaic-layouts now list next as a peer dependency. Your site must depend on next directly, which it normally does already.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
headings: 1. Find where each file has moved
records.text: | Pages Router site | App Router site | | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | src/pages/_app.tsx | src/app/layout.tsx (HTML shell, fonts, global CSS, site-wide metadata ) and src/app/providers.tsx (provider stack) | | src/pages/_document.tsx | src/app/layout.tsx | | src/pages/[...route].tsx | src/app/[namespace]/[...route]/page.tsx | | src/pages/index.tsx (redirect) | src/app/page.tsx | | src/pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts | src/auth.ts and src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts | | src/pages/api/content/preview.ts | src/app/[namespace]/[...route]/previewAction.ts (Server Action) | | Browser WebSocket to the CLI's /workflows | src/app/[namespace]/[...route]/persistAction.ts (Server Action) and src/app/api/workflows/[jobId]/events/route.ts | | components object in _app.tsx | src/app/[namespace]/[...route]/MdxComponents.ts | | Metadata component with next/head | generateMetadata in src/app/[namespace]/[...route]/page.tsx | | src/types/mosaic.ts | Removed | | .eslintrc.js | eslint.config.mjs | | .env.local (committed) | .env.development | | .env.prod | .env.production | The new site also adds files that have no Pages Router equivalent: [namespace]/layout.tsx , which loads the data shared by a namespace ( /mosaic/... ) once and keeps the header mounted while readers navigate (see Providers, theme and layouts ) [namespace]/page.tsx , which renders paths with no segments after the namespace, such as /mosaic and root-level documents like /about , with the catch-all's page. Use a required catch-all ( [...route] ), not an optional one ( [[...route]] ): Next.js treats an optional catch-all whose only value is index as empty, so /mosaic/index was served from the /mosaic page and the header's prefetch of it repeated without end on 404 pages not-found.tsx , [namespace]/not-found.tsx , error.tsx and global-error.tsx robots.ts and sitemap.ts api/revalidate/route.ts , which clears cached content when the CLI reports an update api/content/live and api/content/ready , which reload pages in next dev when content changes, including pages that returned 404 while the CLI was still loading next.config.js is now split into a base config, a config used only when the site runs on a server, and a config for static export. If your site uses the content editor, copy experimental.serverActions.bodySizeLimit from the reference next.config.js . Next.js rejects Server Action requests over 1 MB by default, so without it saves of large pages fail before they reach the CLI.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: The old _app.tsx merged your components into components and passed them to every page. Add them to hostComponents in src/app/[namespace]/[...route]/MdxComponents.ts instead: The file is marked 'use client' , so the components it registers must work in the browser.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: _app.tsx wrapped every page in a single provider stack, so the header and the rest of the frame stayed mounted between pages. The App Router site splits that into three parts: Providers ( src/app/providers.tsx ) wraps the whole site and is mounted once by layout.tsx . It holds ColorModeProvider and ThemeProvider , plus the session provider and Mosaic auth adapter when authentication is enabled. NamespaceFrame ( src/app/[namespace]/NamespaceFrame.tsx ) is mounted by [namespace]/layout.tsx and stays mounted while readers navigate under the same leading URL segment. It loads the frame's shared config and search index once and renders the header. A page passes its canonical content route, shared config (per-folder header overrides) and edit state to the header with <FrameSync> . Relative links and images use the canonical route even when the browser is visiting an alias. StoreShell ( src/app/providers.tsx ) wraps each page and is mounted by page.tsx . It holds the page's store, BaseUrlProvider , ImageProvider , LinkProvider and LayoutProvider . Layouts leave the header out because NamespaceFrame renders it. To add your own layouts, replace mosaicLayouts in StoreShell with { ...mosaicLayouts, MyLayout } . Import global CSS and fonts in layout.tsx . Salt adds its component styles and its theme settings (density, accent, corners and fonts) in the browser, after the page hydrates. Without them in the server HTML, every page changes size as it hydrates. The reference layout.tsx adds them to the server HTML, and your layout.tsx should do the same: Import @salt-ds/core/css/salt-core.css and @salt-ds/icons/css/salt-icon.css before @jpmorganchase/mosaic-site-preset-styles/index.css , so Mosaic's styles still override Salt's. Set data-accent , data-corner , data-heading-font and data-action-font on <html> , with the values ThemeProvider passes to Salt. Use the inline theme script from src/lib/themePrefScript.ts . It sets data-mode and Salt's density class before the first paint. The optional catch-all also renders single-segment documents and aliases, such as /about or /quickstart . The first URL segment is only a boundary for the persistent frame; it does not have to match a source's namespace or prefixDir . Folder index URLs continue to resolve through the content loaders. The sidebar stays with each page so it follows updated content. Initial server HTML uses the layout's fallback config and the index route associated with that config. <FrameSync> applies the page's canonical route and config before the first client paint; layouts do not receive their child page's route data. Without authentication, omit both auth providers. Mosaic's auth hook defaults to signed out with login disabled; it makes no session requests: For Auth.js, mount NextAuthAdapter inside SessionProvider . This is a required migration: an existing SessionProvider alone no longer connects Mosaic's UI to the session. The reference host mounts this pair only when AUTH_ENABLED is true. It leaves the session unresolved on the server and fetches it after mount: If omitted, the adapter's loginEnabled prop follows NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_LOGIN . It supplies the session user, loading status, sign-in/sign-out actions and a stable sign-in link. Other authentication systems can provide the structural MosaicAuthValue through MosaicAuthProvider from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-site-components/auth . This context controls UI only: keep write authorization on the server.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: Snapshots use 0.0.0-snapshot-<timestamp> intentionally, so they do not satisfy ordinary ^0.1.0-beta.x ranges. Install one exact snapshot version for all of the host's Mosaic packages. Extensions should use peer dependencies and externalize them, rather than installing their own Mosaic runtime. At the host's package root, pin each Mosaic package in its dependency graph to the same snapshot using Yarn resolutions . For example, this excerpt uses the published 0.0.0-snapshot-20261115213905 cohort: Repeat the resolution for every Mosaic package used directly or transitively; the two entries above illustrate the syntax. That older snapshot does not contain all changes in this guide: choose a cohort containing the fixes you need. Yarn can still warn that an extension's normal-release peer range excludes the snapshot. Test that extension against the preview and explicitly support the tested version when needed; do not permanently widen published peer ranges to every snapshot merely to silence warnings.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: getServerSideProps and the middleware chain ( createMiddlewareRunner , middlewarePresets ) are gone. Fetch your data in src/app/[namespace]/[...route]/page.tsx instead: Write an async function that loads the data. Wrap it in React's cache() if generateMetadata also needs it, so it runs once per request. Call it inside the existing Promise.all next to resolveContent . Search is loaded independently by the header through the records API or browser index. Pass the result to your component as a prop, or add it to storeProps and read it with useStore from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-store . Snapshot builds pre-render pages, so this function runs at build time there.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: generateMetadata in page.tsx builds the title, description and Open Graph tags from frontmatter. Add per-page tags there, and site-wide tags to the metadata export in layout.tsx . Don't add the old Metadata component back; it would duplicate every tag.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: Replace next/router with next/navigation ( useRouter , usePathname , useSearchParams ), and add 'use client' to the top of the file. Components that use hooks, context or browser APIs need 'use client' , either in their own file or in the file that imports them. router.events doesn't exist in the App Router, so useIsLoading and Fade have been removed. Don't call useSearchParams() in components that render on pre-rendered pages. It makes Next.js render those pages in the browser instead. To check whether the editor is open, use useIsEditing() from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-content-editor-plugin/useEditMode .

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: Move each src/pages/api/<name>.ts handler to src/app/api/<name>/route.ts , exporting GET , POST and so on, using the web Request and Response types. If you use static export, add your route to ROUTES in scripts/static-export-route-stubs.mjs . Next.js won't export a route handler unless it is marked as static, and that script does this for you during build:static:* . To serve your docs as Markdown for agents ( /llms.txt and /<page>.md ), copy src/app/api/llms/[...path]/route.ts , its rewrites in next.config.js and its entry in scripts/static-export-route-stubs.mjs from the reference site. See LlmsTxtPlugin .

records.text: src/auth.ts holds the Auth.js configuration, and src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts exports its handlers. On the server, call auth() instead of getServerSession() . Rename NEXTAUTH_SECRET to AUTH_SECRET . The old name still works. Generate a secret with openssl rand -base64 32 . Remove NEXTAUTH_URL . The site trusts the request's host instead. Set MOSAIC_AUTH_ENABLED=true to turn sign-in on. GITHUB_ID , GITHUB_SECRET and the GitHub callback URL ( /api/auth/callback/github ) haven't changed. Set MOSAIC_EDITORS . It lists who may sign in and edit: comma-separated emails, @domains , or * . Emails and @domains only match email addresses that GitHub has verified. If it isn't set, nobody can sign in in production. Set MOSAIC_EDITORS=* to keep the old behaviour, where anyone who could sign in could edit. records.text: The editor only appears on pages from a writable source. A source must declare capabilities: { writable: true } . source-git-repo does; source-local-folder , source-http and the other read-only sources don't. If you wrote your own source and want it to be editable, add capabilities to it. Frontmatter can't turn editing on. Preview and save now run on the site's server. The browser no longer connects to the CLI. Replace NEXT_PUBLIC_MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_URL with MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_URL , which is only read on the server. Saves no longer use WebSockets. Set MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_URL to the CLI's base HTTP URL, such as http://mosaic-fs:8080 . The site starts a save with an HTTP request to the CLI, and the editor follows its progress with Server-Sent Events through the site's /api/workflows/<jobId>/events route. An old ws://…/workflows value still works, but logs a warning. Set MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_SECRET to the same value on the site and the CLI. If the CLI doesn't have it, no save will run. Saves that take longer than MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_TIMEOUT_MS (set on the CLI, 5 minutes by default) are reported as failed. Authors can create new pages from the editor. In next dev , MOSAIC_DEV_BYPASS_CAPABILITY_GATE=true shows the editor on every page. It has no effect in production.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: | Before | Now | Why | | ------------ | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | .env.local | .env.development | Next.js loads .env.local in production too. Only next dev loads .env.development , so its placeholder secrets and dev-only flags can't reach a production build. | | .env.prod | .env.production | Next.js never loaded .env.prod . It loads .env.production for next build and next start . | Don't commit real secrets to either file. Set them in your hosting environment, or in .env.local or .env.production.local , which git ignores. If your mosaic.config.mjs loads env files with @next/env , only load the development files when asked to: loadEnvConfig(projectDir, process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development') . Then set NODE_ENV=development in the scripts that run the CLI locally, as the reference site's serve , debug and gen:snapshot scripts do. Otherwise a mosaic serve started without NODE_ENV would pick up the placeholder secrets from .env.development . Production builds now default to snapshot mode. .env.production sets MOSAIC_MODE=snapshot-file . If your site reads content from a running Mosaic CLI, set MOSAIC_MODE=active explicitly. Values set in the environment take precedence over .env.production . Both the site and the CLI check their variables when they start. A production site ( next start or the standalone server.js ) and mosaic serve exit with code 1 on an invalid value, and list every problem as NAME: reason ; next dev only logs the list. next build doesn't check runtime variables, so you can still build an image without them. Copy src/instrumentation.ts and src/lib/config.ts from the reference site to get the site checks. The full lists, with types and defaults, are in the site README and the Admin page. snapshot-s3 mode is removed. MOSAIC_MODE is now active or snapshot-file , and the reference site refuses to start or build with any other value. If you kept snapshots in S3, download the snapshot folder before you build (for example aws s3 sync s3://your-bucket snapshots/latest ), then set MOSAIC_MODE=snapshot-file and point MOSAIC_SNAPSHOT_DIR at that folder, relative to the site's folder. The build:static:s3 and serve:snapshot:s3 scripts are gone too; use build:static:file and serve:snapshot:file .

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: The /workflows WebSocket is gone. Saves start with POST /workflows/jobs and report progress as Server-Sent Events from GET /workflows/jobs/:jobId/events . See Workflows . CORS is off by default. The CLI used to allow every origin. The site calls the CLI from its server, so it doesn't need CORS. Only set MOSAIC_CORS_ORIGINS if a browser calls the CLI directly. The admin API needs a secret outside development. Only /_mosaic_/tags/list stays open. If an SSO proxy in front of the CLI uses the Authorization header, send the secret in x-mosaic-admin-secret . mosaic build empties the snapshot folder ( --out joined with --name ) before writing it, so deleted pages no longer linger. It rejects a --name that points at the output folder itself or outside it, such as . or ../x . mosaic upload is removed , with its -S / --snapshot option. If you still want a copy of your snapshots in S3, upload the folder yourself, for example with aws s3 sync snapshots/latest s3://your-bucket . Sources now honour requestTimeout . The HTTP, Readme, Storybook and Figma sources apply it, and it defaults to 5 seconds. Raise requestTimeout for any source that regularly takes longer to respond.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: Docker: the reference Dockerfiles use Node.js 24 and set MOSAIC_MODE=active in both the build and run stages. Do the same in your own images if they read from a running CLI. They also set MOSAIC_OUTPUT=standalone in the build stage, which makes next.config.js emit the .next/standalone server they copy into the runtime image. Network: only the site's server needs to reach the CLI, through MOSAIC_ACTIVE_MODE_URL and MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_URL , over plain HTTP. You no longer need to expose the CLI to browsers or allow WebSockets. Proxies must not buffer text/event-stream responses, from the CLI or from the site's /api/workflows/ routes. If you run several CLI instances, a save's progress must be read from the instance that started it. Static export (optional): yarn build:static:file builds a fully static out/ folder that any CDN can serve. See Static export . Security headers: the reference next.config.js sends Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self' , X-Frame-Options , X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy , and turns off X-Powered-By . Copy them into your config. A static export ignores next.config.js headers, so set them in your hosting layer instead. If other sites embed your pages, add their origins to frame-ancestors . Snapshots: rebuild your snapshots with the new mosaic build . Prerender routes: regenerate snapshots to include mosaic-routes.json . Use generateMosaicStaticParams({ pageExtensions: ['.mdx'] }) from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-site-middleware/routes instead of deriving static params from loadSitemap() . Keep the required catch-all/root-page split; the helper returns both forms. Sitemap exclusions now affect SEO only. See snapshot route inventory for selection, empty-host and legacy-snapshot behavior.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: Use Node.js 24 or later. Upgrade all @jpmorganchase/mosaic-* packages to the same version. Auth.js hosts also upgrade next-auth to v5 and mount NextAuthAdapter inside SessionProvider . Export the current packages/site using Create a Site and move your components, layouts, CSS and config into it. Replace next/router imports and move pages/api handlers to app/api route handlers. Rename .env.local to .env.development and .env.prod to .env.production , and rename the env vars listed above. Set AUTH_SECRET , MOSAIC_AUTH_ENABLED and MOSAIC_EDITORS on the site. Set the same MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_SECRET on the site and the CLI. Set MOSAIC_ADMIN_SECRET , and MOSAIC_CORS_ORIGINS if needed, on the CLI. Set MOSAIC_MODE=active if your site reads from a running CLI, or MOSAIC_MODE=snapshot-file if it used snapshot-s3 . Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL when you build the site. Run yarn build && yarn start , open a few pages, sign in, then edit and save a page from a Git source.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: The default header now uses section-level search. Remove getSearchData , useSearchIndex , and the searchIndex / searchConfig store props from custom integrations. Regenerate snapshots: the three legacy search files are no longer emitted. Server sites use /api/search ; static exports use a lazy browser index from search-records.json . See search configuration for provider and plugin migration details.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: App Router hosts can import buildMosaicMetadata from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-site-middleware/metadata and pass the result of resolveContent . It returns document title, description, canonical URL and the historic lastModified/breadcrumb meta tags; missing documents and redirects return an empty object. This module is pure and does not load content. Keep metadataBase , Open Graph/Twitter branding and image policy in your host. The /client entrypoint exports CanonicalizeUrl and LiveReload . Mount CanonicalizeUrl only after the host's folder/index check; arbitrary aliases should keep their URL. It preserves the router's history state, query and hash. LiveReload refreshes the Next router on each content change and accepts an endpoint (default /api/content/live ) and optional onContentChanged callback for host-owned caches. Render it only in development. Node route adapters can use these narrow server imports: The host must apply its own placeholder/production secret policy in getSecret ; an absent secret fails closed with 503, and invalid credentials return 401. The webhook accepts x-mosaic-revalidate-secret or a Bearer token, immediately expires the content cache tag, then notifies connected development clients only after invalidation succeeds. The /live-reload/bus entrypoint exports notifyContentChanged and subscribeContentChanged for custom Node adapters. This bus is local to one process and survives development HMR; it is not a cross-process or distributed messaging service. Streams clean up on request abort, cancellation and failed writes. Static-export hosts must omit/stub these runtime routes, as the reference host already does.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: A custom App Router host can import NamespaceFrame and StoreShell from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-layouts/host , with FrameSync from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-store/frame . Mount the namespace frame in the persistent layout, then put a shell and sync component in each page: In a real App Router tree the frame and page shell belong to different route files. Keep one root ColorModeProvider above them. NamespaceFrame accepts the same image/link renderer slots as StoreShell ; its optional header defaults to Mosaic's app header. StoreShell also forwards defaultLayout and LayoutProps . These slots are client-side composition: import custom components in a client wrapper rather than passing component functions across the server boundary. The fallback configuration must be paired with its canonical document route, including /index . FrameSync applies page route/config/edit overrides before paint without replacing the header. Render <FrameSync /> on a missing page to restore the latest namespace fallback. It is harmless outside a frame. Frame fallbacks and page seeds have different lifetimes; do not reseed the persistent frame with fallback data on each render. Hosts supplying their own composition can use useMosaicStore(seed) and StoreProvider directly. The hook creates one store per instance, keeps its identity across renders, and replaces page data before paint when the seed object identity changes. Omitted fields reset to their defaults; provide a new seed object when refreshing data. The legacy useCreateStore API is unchanged. Server layouts may import colorModeScript from the pure @jpmorganchase/mosaic-store/theme-preference subpath and render it in an inline head script before hydration. This subpath also exports STORAGE_KEY , parseColorModePreference and serializeColorModePreference . The stored format remains { state: { colorMode: 'light' | 'dark' }, version: 0 } ; missing, malformed or blocked storage boots in light mode. The script sets only data-mode ; density and other host preferences remain in the host. Continue following your host's script nonce/CSP policy.

records.title: Migrate to the App Router
records.text: The packed consumer checks Mosaic's public declarations with skipLibCheck: false . Its Next hosts use TypeScript 6.0.3 because Next 16.4 currently emits DOM types missing from TypeScript 5.x ( upstream issue ); Mosaic's library build remains on TypeScript 5.9. Auth.js 5.0.0-beta.32 currently ships separate declaration defects, including React's removed global JSX namespace and missing internal type exports. The installed-auth runtime fixture therefore mounts the real SessionProvider in a small JavaScript bootstrap, with a separate strict TypeScript contract for Mosaic's public NextAuthAdapter . The browser still verifies authenticated rendering and hydration. This validates Mosaic's declarations and Auth.js runtime integration; it does not certify Auth.js's own declarations or replace them with shims. TypeScript hosts importing SessionProvider directly may encounter those upstream diagnostics until Auth.js fixes them.

records.title: Publish a site to Vercel
records.text: As the vercel platform hosts static content you will need to deploy a mosaic snapshot. There is no option to run mosaic in active mode .

records.title: Publish a site to Vercel
records.text: Mosaic supports two production builds in snapshot-file mode: Default SSR build — yarn build + yarn start (or Vercel's default Next.js runtime). Pages are pre-rendered at build time via generateStaticParams but the Node runtime stays in the deployment so the /api/* route handlers (auth, content-editor preview, cache revalidation webhook) keep working. Fully static export — yarn build:static:file . Emits a CDN-shippable out/ directory with no Node runtime needed. The /api/* route handlers are replaced with 501 stubs at build time (see scripts/static-export-route-stubs.mjs for the why), so this target is for read-only sites with no auth and no in-browser content editor. The instructions below assume the default SSR build. For the static target, point your hosting at out/ instead of letting Vercel build Next normally.

records.title: Publish a site to Vercel
records.text: Add the following to the next config file used by your site: Output File Tracing is a feature of Next.js that uses static analysis to determine what files are needed to deploy a production version of an application. Due to the architecture of mosaic, snapshot files can be ignored by this process and therefore excluded from the build artifacts deployed by vercel.

records.title: Publish a site to Vercel
records.text: Set 2 environment variables in the vercel dashboard. | Variable Name | Value | | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | | MOSAIC_MODE | snapshot-file | | MOSAIC_SNAPSHOT_DIR | snapshots/latest | | NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL | https://your-site.example.com (no trailing slash) |

records.title: Publish a site to Vercel
records.text: This is the canonical origin of the deployed site. It is read at build/render time by: app/layout.tsx — sets Next's metadataBase , which is what turns relative og:image / twitter:image URLs in your per-page metadata into absolute URLs that social-card unfurlers (Slack, X, LinkedIn, Discord, iMessage, etc.) can actually resolve. app/sitemap.ts — emits absolute <loc> entries in /sitemap.xml . app/robots.ts — emits the absolute Sitemap: line in /robots.txt . Set this per environment : Production: your real public hostname, e.g. https://docs.example.com . Preview deployments: Vercel exposes NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_URL for each preview. Either set NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL per preview, or wire it up in next.config.js to fall back to https://${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_VERCEL_URL} when unset. Local dev: falls back to http://localhost:3000 automatically if unset. If the variable is missing in a production build the site still works, but absolute URLs in metadata/sitemap/robots will fall back to localhost and social cards / SEO will be broken. The site logs a warning at boot in that case. If it is set but isn't an absolute http(s) URL, the site refuses to start.

records.title: Admin
records.text: There are several admin urls exposed by Mosaic that provide an insight into how the filesystem has been configured and a way to remotely manage sources.

records.title: Admin
records.text: | Endpoint | Method | Description | Params | | ------------------------------ | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | | /_mosaic_/config | GET | Returns the JSON from the Mosaic config file | n/a | | /_mosaic_/content/dump | GET | Returns the entire mosaic filesystem as JSON | n/a | | /_mosaic_/sources/list | GET | Returns a collection of active sources | n/a | | /_mosaic_/source/add | POST | Adds the source | definition & isPreview | | /_mosaic_/source/stop | PUT | Stops the source with the provided name | name | | /_mosaic_/source/restart | PUT | Restarts the source with the provided name | name | | /_mosaic_/tags/list | GET | Returns the tag names known to the filesystem | n/a | | /_mosaic_/webhooks/bitbucket | POST | Refreshes git repo sources when Bitbucket reports a push | Bitbucket push event |

records.title: Admin
records.text: Every endpoint except /_mosaic_/tags/list and /_mosaic_/webhooks/bitbucket can reveal or change server state, so they are protected by MOSAIC_ADMIN_SECRET on the CLI process: Secret set: requests must send it. Opening an endpoint in a browser shows a login prompt; enter any username and the secret as the password. From scripts, send it as a bearer token (or in an x-mosaic-admin-secret header): Requests without a valid secret get 401 . Secret not set: the endpoints are open when NODE_ENV=development (the reference site's yarn serve and yarn debug scripts set it) and return 403 otherwise, including when NODE_ENV is unset. Basic auth sends the secret base64-encoded, not encrypted, so only use it over HTTPS outside local development.

records.title: Admin
records.text: /_mosaic_/webhooks/bitbucket receives Bitbucket Data Center push events, so git repo sources pick up new commits within seconds instead of at their next scheduled check. Bitbucket can't send the admin secret, so the endpoint checks the webhook's signature instead: it only exists when MOSAIC_BITBUCKET_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set, and rejects requests that aren't signed with it ( 401 ). See Refresh on push for the setup.

records.title: Admin
records.text: The editor's save workflow runs over plain HTTP, with progress streamed as Server-Sent Events (SSE). No WebSocket is needed. The workflows use the server's repository credentials, so every request must send the CLI's MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_SECRET as a bearer token (or in an x-mosaic-workflows-secret header). Without that variable no workflow runs. The site sends the same value from its own MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_SECRET (see packages/site/README.md ). The placeholder value committed in the site's .env.development is ignored unless NODE_ENV=development . POST /workflows/jobs starts a workflow. The JSON body (up to 5 MB) names the workflow and the user, and carries the page's route and content: It can also carry frontmatter , targetRoute (rename), isNewPage: true (create) and an optional commitMessage override. Messages must be nonblank text, at most 8 KiB of UTF-8, without control characters other than LF or CRLF line endings. CRLF becomes LF. Omit the field to use the source's configured default. The CLI responds 202 { "jobId": "…" } , or with { "error": "…" } and 400 (invalid request), 401 (wrong secret), 404 (page not found), 409 (new page already exists), 413 (too large) or 503 (secret not configured, or too many workflows running). POST /workflows/defaults inspects the selected workflow before saving. It uses the same workflow secret, route normalization and source ownership as /workflows/jobs . The site also checks the signed-in editor before calling it. Its JSON body (up to 16 KiB) contains name , user , route , and optionally targetRoute and isNewPage ; it needs no page content: The response is either { "supportsCommitMessage": true, "commitMessage": "docs: update ..." } or { "supportsCommitMessage": false } . Only these fields are returned, never source options or credentials. The response is not cached. This lookup does not allocate a job, run a workflow action, clone a repository or write content. Custom workflow prepare hooks must also remain side-effect-free. Invalid requests or defaults return 400 , missing pages 404 , conflicting new pages 409 , wrong secrets 401 , oversized requests 413 , and an unconfigured secret 503 . See Editor commit messages for source settings. GET /workflows/jobs/:jobId/events?user=<sid> streams the job's progress as text/event-stream . user must be the user the job was started for, otherwise the response is 404 . Each update is an event: progress with data: { "status", "message" } , and the stream ends with one event: done whose status is SUCCESS (with the workflow's result as message ) or ERROR . Events have ids, so a client that reconnects with Last-Event-ID (or ?lastEventId= ) only gets the events it missed. The CLI sends a : ping comment every 15 seconds to keep proxies from closing the stream. A job fails if it hasn't finished after MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_TIMEOUT_MS (validated when the CLI starts, default 5 minutes). A timeout ends progress reporting, while the workflow can still finish. The same editor cannot retry the workflow for that page until it stops. Check for the result before retrying. Jobs are kept in memory, up to 100 jobs with up to 500 events each, and a finished job is kept for 10 minutes. Jobs are lost when the CLI restarts, so a save in progress at that moment is reported as failed. If you run several CLI instances, a job's events request must reach the instance that started it: point MOSAIC_WORKFLOWS_URL at one instance, or use sticky routing in your load balancer. Proxies in front of the CLI must not buffer text/event-stream responses (the CLI sends X-Accel-Buffering: no for nginx).

records.title: Active mode
records.text: In active mode content can be pulled from heterogeneous data sources and normalized via plugins, to the configured components/theme. As your content changes, the site will re-pull the content and update your site in real-time. The standard generated site comes with 2 sources to demonstrate, how 'active' mode work. a local source, which loads content from ./docs a remote source, which loads content from a sample Github repository

records.title: Active mode
records.text: All content is composed together within a namespace . A namespace is the scope for aggregated content, represented by the root path. e.g Our sample docs are aggregated into a namespace called mosaic and served by the user journey http://localhost:3000/mosaic Mosaic doc sources are defined by a file called mosaic.config.mjs Here is how that might look for a standard site.

records.title: Active mode
records.text: To tryout local content creation, add a file called ./docs/index.mdx The load http://localhost:3000/local Each directory should contain an index.mdx which is the default page, when a page is loaded without a path Now create other pages and subdirectories and explore how Mosaic, builds your user-journeys from your fileset.

records.title: Active mode
records.text: To tryout remote content creation, your standard site comes pre-configured to load our Mosaic sample docs. Edit the mosaic.config.mjs and change your repoUrl and branch to pull content from other repos.

records.title: Modes of operation
records.text: Mosaic can operate in 2 different modes active snapshot-file

records.title: Modes of operation
records.text: In active mode, content updates in real-time. active mode content is pulled at configured intervals in real-time, as defined by mosaic.config.mjs . Read the active configuration docs.

records.title: Modes of operation
records.text: Consider a snapshot as a directory of static content previously pulled from your content sources, which does not update itself. In snapshot mode, the snapshot does not update itself.

records.title: Modes of operation
records.text: In snapshot-file mode, immutable snapshots of content are loaded at startup from the local file-system. Read the snapshot-file configuration docs.

records.title: Modes of operation
records.text: A snapshot-file site can additionally be built as a fully-static site ( out/ directory of HTML) servable from any CDN with no Node runtime. Read the static export docs.

records.title: Snapshot file mode
records.text: In snapshot-file mode a local immutable snapshot can be loaded by the site. Typically, the snapshot and the site are deployed together and upon startup the site can load the snapshot from the local file-system. To use snapshot-file mode

records.title: Snapshot file mode
records.text: To generate a snapshot, run Commit the snapshot to your Git repo and push the site+snapshot to your Git repo, within the same branch. The CLI fails with a nonzero exit code when any source records a plugin exception, including failures caught by the pipeline. Diagnostics identify the source, plugin, lifecycle, and original error. A failed pipeline does not write a completed snapshot or generation identity; fix the reported error and regenerate before deploying.

records.title: Snapshot file mode
records.text: The CLI writes mosaic-snapshot.json at the snapshot root after all content and aliases have been written successfully. This reserved file contains a versioned generation ID: Every completed build gets a new ID, including builds that reuse the same output directory. Deploy this file with the complete snapshot. Mosaic includes the resolved snapshot directory and generation ID in persistent MDX and shared-configuration cache keys, so a new generation does not reuse content cached for an older snapshot. Older snapshots remain readable. If the identity file is missing or invalid, Mosaic skips persistent loader caching while retaining per-request memoization. Regenerate the snapshot with the updated CLI to enable caching; do not reuse an ID for changed content. Snapshots remain immutable deployment artifacts. Publish the complete snapshot with the site rather than overwriting files while requests are reading them. The generation ID affects loader data caching; changing it alone does not invalidate already-rendered Next.js routes. Deploy a new site build or use the appropriate Next.js route revalidation when replacing a snapshot in a running deployment.

records.title: Snapshot file mode
records.text: Every successful mosaic build also writes mosaic-routes.json , independently of SiteMapPlugin and its SEO exclusions. The version 1 envelope contains snapshotId (matching the completion identity) and routes , an array of { pathname, sourcePathname } records. pathname is a percent-encoded URL; sourcePathname is its decoded backing file path, including the extension. Actual files, aliases and supported folder/index shortcuts determine this inventory. A frontmatter route alone does not create a URL. App Router hosts can use the public helper: The helper defaults to MOSAIC_SNAPSHOT_DIR ; pass snapshotDir to choose another directory. It returns decoded { namespace, route } params, where namespace means the first URL segment, not the source's configured namespace. A required [...route] page selects entries with a nonempty route ; a separate [namespace]/page.tsx selects empty routes and returns { namespace } . The host handles / itself. When constructing loader URLs from Next's decoded params, encode each segment with encodeURIComponent . pageExtensions explicitly selects backing documents the host can render. Core may also admit JSON or custom data files, which should not automatically become MDX pages. include(record) can further restrict prerendering without changing SEO output. The reference site selects .mdx files. Custom extension inventory does not add new loader behavior: explicit /index still resolves to .mdx , and folder shortcuts need an existing extensionless index alias. An empty CLI inventory is valid, including builds with zero enabled sources. The host helper rejects an empty selection by default; set allowEmpty: true for an intentionally empty host. Missing, malformed, unsupported or mismatched inventory/identity files fail with a regeneration message. Existing content loaders can still read older snapshots, but adopting this helper requires regenerating them. It never falls back to the SEO sitemap.

records.title: Static export
records.text: When you run a Mosaic site in snapshot-file mode, all of its content is fixed at build time. That means you can pre-render every page to plain HTML and serve the result from any static host — no Node.js runtime required. The Mosaic site ships a build script that produces a fully-static out/ directory from a local snapshot directory: The command sets MOSAIC_OUTPUT=export and MOSAIC_MODE=snapshot-file , then invokes next build . The output is a self-contained out/ directory you can upload to S3, Vercel static, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, or any other static host.

records.title: Static export
records.text: Every page enumerated by the snapshot's sitemap.xml (typically every doc in your sources). robots.txt and sitemap.xml . All static assets from public/ , including the snapshot's search-records.json . Stubbed app/api/* route handlers that return HTTP 501. These exist only because Next.js refuses to emit a static export when the route files are present but cannot be statically pre-rendered; the stubs are applied automatically before the build and reverted afterwards. You cannot use the auth, preview, revalidate, or search API routes in a static export.

records.title: Static export
headings: What does not work in a static export
records.text: | Feature | Reason | Workaround | | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | active mode | Active mode reads content from a live Mosaic server on every request | Use snapshot-file for the export build | | next.config.js redirects() | Not supported by output: 'export' | Configure redirects at the hosting layer (S3 redirects, CloudFront Functions, Vercel vercel.json , Nginx, etc.) | | /api/auth/* (Auth.js) | Auth.js needs a server | Auth-gated sites must run in the regular (non-export) build | | /api/content/preview | Same — needs a server | Editor preview requires the regular build | | /api/revalidate | Same — no ISR in a static export | Re-run the build to publish content changes | | /api/search | Same — needs a server | Search /search-records.json in the browser with @jpmorganchase/mosaic-site-middleware/search | | next/image optimisation | Disabled in export builds | Images are served as-is ( images.unoptimized: true ) | If your site relies on any of these features, deploy the regular Node build instead. See the publish guide .

records.title: Static export
headings: How the export build is configured
records.text: The exact knobs live in packages/site/next.config.js and packages/site/package.json . Three things differ from the regular build: A separate config branch. next.config.js switches on process.env.MOSAIC_OUTPUT === 'export' to emit output: 'export' , set images.unoptimized: true , and drop redirects() . The config throws loudly if you try to combine MOSAIC_OUTPUT=export with active mode. generateStaticParams enumerates routes from the sitemap. The catch-all page ( app/[namespace]/[...route]/page.tsx ) reads the snapshot's sitemap.xml at build time and emits one static page per entry. In non-snapshot builds it short-circuits to a fully-dynamic route. API route and Server Action stubs. scripts/static-export-route-stubs.mjs backs up each route.ts and Server Action module to <file>.bak and writes a static stub (HTTP 501 + literal dynamic = 'force-static' for routes, a throwing function for actions) before the build, and restores the originals afterwards — even if the build fails. If a build is interrupted, run yarn build:static:revert to restore manually. Because there is no server to load it on demand, the 404 page's header data is read at build time instead.

records.title: Static export
records.text: The out/ directory is a flat tree of .html , .js , .css , image, and font files. Any of the following will serve it correctly: Note: static hosts typically need try_files $uri $uri.html (or the equivalent) so that /mosaic/index resolves to mosaic/index.html without an explicit .html suffix in the URL.

records.title: $AliasPlugin
records.text: The $AliasPlugin is what powers the aliases feature of Mosaic. It does this by scrapes aliases from page metadata and also applies all aliases stored in config.data.aliases Other plugins can use setAliases to apply new aliases, as long as they call it before this plugin has reaches the $beforeSend lifecycle event. This plugin is added to the plugins collection by Mosaic itself so users do not need to include it in their own mosaic config file.

records.title: $AliasPlugin
records.text: This plugin runs with a priority of -1 so it runs after most other plugins.

records.title: BreadcrumbsPlugin
records.text: The BreadcrumbsPlugin is responsible for generating the data needed to show breadcrumbs navigation on pages. It then appends this data to a breadcrumbs property in the page metadata. Should a page already have a breadcrumbs property in it's metadata then it is respected and not overwritten. If a page has a sidebar.groupLabel property in it's metadata then this is used as the label for the breadcrumb, otherwise the page title is used. When the BreadcrumbsPlugin is traversing up directories, it needs to know what page in the directory represents the breadcrumb for that directory. It is recommended to use the index page for this but the page to use is a configurable option of the breadcrumbs plugin.

records.title: BreadcrumbsPlugin
records.text: This plugin runs with no special priority.

records.title: BrokenLinksPlugin
records.text: The BrokenLinksPlugin will identify any broken links in pages Mosaic has pulled into it's filesystem by making use of the check-links package. It can identify broken links between the pages themselves and external links that pages link out to. What this plugin is really checking is "liveness" of a link. alive if the URL is reachable (2XX status code) dead if the URL is not reachable invalid if the URL was parsed as invalid or used an unsupported protocol Links may be "alive", but the content of the linked page may not be what you want so continue to check links show what you expect. Links are checked in the background after a source loads, at most four pages at a time, so checking doesn't delay content updates. Broken links, and pages that couldn't be checked, are logged to the console.

records.title: Plugins
records.text: Mosaic Plugins are lifecycle-based hooks that are called on every source at different stages. You will never need to invoke a lifecycle method directly as their execution is managed by a plugin runner. Plugins enable Mosaic to have a lightweight and flexible, modular architecture by encapsulating features and functionality as plugins. Sites can add their own plugins too. See Write a plugin .

records.title: Plugins
records.text: Plugins are added to the plugins collection of the mosaic config file. Like sources , plugins have an options property that can be used to provide plugin specific configuration. | Property | Description | Required | | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | | modulePath | The path to the installed plugin module | Yes | | disabled | Exclude this plugin completely. Defaults to false | No | | runtimeOnly | Exclude this plugin when generating a snapshot. Defaults to false | No | | previewDisabled | Exclude this plugin for "preview" sources | No | | allowMultiple | Allow multiple instances of this plugin to run. | No | | priority | The importance of this plugin. Plugins with the highest priority run first | No | | options | Collection of other configuration values | No | There is no need to import the plugin module directly. As long as the plugin is installed, Mosaic will be able to import it using the built-in plugin loader.

records.text: Should a plugin fail, the failure will not cause a source to close or for any other plugin to not run. Instead plugin errors are tracked by Mosaic and can be viewed in the pluginErrors property available on each source listed by the list sources admin API . Plugin errors will be split by lifecycle event and only the lifecycle events used by the loaded plugins used will be shown.

It then adds a hook, so that when a page is requested the data is loaded from disk and combined with what is already in the Mosaic filesystem. It must be the very last to run so that it can strip off metadata and content after other plugins have finished with them.

records.title: LlmsTxtPlugin
records.text: The LlmsTxtPlugin writes the site's docs as Markdown, for coding agents and other tools that read docs as text. It follows the llms.txt convention, and outputs 3 files: llms.txt : an index of the pages, with a section for each folder and each page's description llms-full.txt : every page in one file markdown-pages.json : every page's Markdown, keyed by route Each page's Markdown starts with frontmatter (its title, description and URL) and a link to llms.txt . In the page body: {meta.*} expressions are replaced with their values, and other expressions and import / export statements are left out. Callout becomes a quote, such as > **Warning:** … . Other components are replaced with their children. A component with no children, such as an example preview, is left out. To convert your own components, see Convert your components . Relative links are made absolute, so they still work in llms-full.txt . To leave a page out, set llms: { exclude: true } in its frontmatter, or match it with the exclude option.

records.title: LlmsTxtPlugin
records.text: The reference site serves the files with createLlmsHandler , from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-site-middleware , at /api/llms/[...path] , and rewrites these URLs to it: | URL | Responds with | | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | | /llms.txt , /llms-full.txt | The file | | /<page>.md | The page's Markdown. A folder serves its index page | | /<page> , with an Accept: text/markdown header | The page's Markdown | The afterFiles rewrites go after public/ and before the site's catch-all page. In snapshot builds, next.config.js copies the files to public/ , so they're served as static files without running a function. Static exports serve only those copies. In active mode, the handler reads the files from the CLI, and checks for new ones every 30 seconds while serving the ones it has. Set maxAge to change that.

records.title: LlmsTxtPlugin
records.text: Set componentsModulePath to a module whose default export converts your components, by name. Each converter gets the element's name, attributes, children (already converted to Markdown) and whether it's inline, and the page's frontmatter. It returns Markdown, null to leave the element out, or undefined to keep its children. Attributes are text, true for an attribute without a value, or { expression } with the source of an expression such as size={2} . A converter that throws leaves its page out, and the plugin reports the error.

records.title: LlmsTxtPlugin
records.text: The default config runs this plugin at priority -1.5 , after $RefPlugin ( -1 ), so $ref s are resolved, and before LazyPagePlugin ( -2 ) moves page content out.

records.title: $RefPlugin
records.text: The $RefPlugin powers the refs feature of Mosaic. The plugin scrapes $ref properties from page metadata and also applies all refs stored in config.data.refs . Other plugins can use config.setRef to apply new refs, as long as they call it before this plugin has reaches $beforeSend .

records.title: SearchIndexPlugin
records.text: The SearchIndexPlugin generates search-records.json for section-level search. The same records and ranking engine power the server API and browser search on static sites.

records.title: SearchIndexPlugin
records.text: search-records.json splits every page into records: one for the text before the first section heading, and one for each section. Results can then link to the section that matched, at route#anchor . The anchors are the ids of the rendered headings, and match the TableOfContentsPlugin . headings lists the section's headings from the outermost in. The introduction record has none. text is the section's prose. Code blocks, JSX attributes and MDX expressions are left out, except {meta.*} expressions, which are replaced with their values. fields holds the frontmatter set with the records.fields option, as plain text without markdown. Only the introduction record has it, because it describes the whole page. All configured fields are searchable: description and keywords have their dedicated ranking, and other field names rank alongside body text. To leave a page out of the records, set search: { exclude: true } in its frontmatter.

records.title: SearchIndexPlugin
records.text: @jpmorganchase/mosaic-site-middleware/search searches the records. It runs on the server and in the browser. Results are ranked like Algolia's tie-breaking criteria. Each one only decides between results that tie on the ones before it: The number of query words matched. Only results that match the most words are returned, so adding a word narrows the results. The page title matching the whole query. Plurals, stop words and spaces are ignored, so datepicker matches "Date picker". The current namespace, set with the namespace search option. The number of typos. Words of 4 letters or more can have one typo, and words of 8 or more two. The number of words matched by a synonym. Where the words matched: the title, then keywords, headings, description, then text and any other configured frontmatter fields. A match on only the start of a word counts one place lower, so for select a title starting "Selectable" ties with the keyword "Select". The section heading matching the whole query. The pageRank option. The page introduction before its sections, and outer sections before inner ones. The relevance score (BM25). | Index option | Description | | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | synonyms | Groups of single words that mean the same thing. Matches of a synonym rank just below matches of the word itself. | | groupBy | Records with the same group are one result: the best match, with the other matches in sections . Defaults to the route. Group tabs of a page together here. | | pageRank | Ranks pages when everything else ties: lower comes first. Defaults to 0 for index pages and 1 for others. | | Search option | Description | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | namespace | Results in this namespace rank above equally good results. | | namespaces | Only return results in these namespaces. | | filter | Only return records this function returns true for. | | limit | The most results to return. Defaults to 10 . | | sectionsPerResult | The most other matching sections per result. Defaults to 3 . | highlight(text, result.terms) splits a title or snippet into matching and other parts, to render the matches without using HTML from the index.

records.title: SearchIndexPlugin
records.text: createSearchHandler from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-site-middleware is a GET route handler that searches the site's records on the server: GET /api/search?q=date+picker&namespace=salt responds with { query, results } . | Parameter | Description | | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | q | The query. Longer than 200 characters is cut. | | namespace | Rank results in this namespace first. | | namespaces | Only return results in these namespaces, comma-separated. | | limit | The most results, from 1 to the handler's maxLimit (50 by default). Defaults to 10. | | sections | The most other matching sections per result, from 0 to 10. Defaults to 3. | The handler takes the index options above, and: mode and contentUrl , which default to MOSAIC_MODE and its content URL. maxAge : in active mode, how long in milliseconds to use the loaded records before checking the content server for new ones. Searches use the loaded records until the check finishes. Defaults to 30 seconds. In snapshot mode, the handler checks the file's modification time on every search. maxLimit : the most results a request can ask for. Defaults to 50. The handler keeps the index in memory rather than in Next's data cache, which doesn't store entries over 2 MB. It responds with 404 when the site has no search-records.json , and 503 when the records can't be loaded. Static exports have no server, so they search in the browser instead: the reference site copies search-records.json to public/ when it builds from a snapshot.

records.title: SearchIndexPlugin
records.text: The default header uses the search API. It fetches results after the reader types, displays matching sections, and links directly to their headings. It does not load a search index into the page store. Wrap a custom site's client provider tree with SearchProvider from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-site-components/SearchProvider : For static exports, use mode="browser" and copy search-records.json into public/ . The browser downloads the records and search engine on the first nonempty query and reuses the index across queries and navigation: The reference site selects the mode automatically from MOSAIC_OUTPUT . Custom sites can set namespace to prefer a namespace, or enabled={false} to hide search when records are disabled. Server mode is the default without a provider. Endpoint and records URLs can be configured for a site's base path.

records.title: SearchIndexPlugin
records.text: The legacy search-data.json , search-data-condensed.json , and search-config.json outputs and Fuse-based UI are removed. Regenerate existing snapshots with the updated CLI. Remove legacy public-asset copies and maxLineLength , maxLineCount , keys , and relevancy from plugin options; use records.fields , records.maxTextLength , and the search engine options documented above instead. Ranking uses the new engine's defined order rather than Fuse weights. Remove getSearchData calls, useSearchIndex , and searchIndex / searchConfig store props. Custom UIs can use createSearchHandler or createSearchIndex directly; the built-in header needs only the provider configuration above. SearchIndex , SearchConfig , and SearchIndexSlice are no longer exported by the store. Move any old header searchNamespace setting to SearchProvider 's namespace prop.

records.title: SearchIndexPlugin
records.text: The provider accepts queryOptions in both modes. For example, queryOptions={{ limit: 20, sectionsPerResult: 0 }} requests up to 20 results without additional section lists. Defaults remain six results and three sections. The server handler's maxLimit and section cap still apply. In browser mode, indexOptions configures the same engine as createSearchIndex : For server mode, configure groupBy , pageRank , and synonyms on createSearchHandler({ ...indexOptions }) in the API route. Provider indexOptions only configure the browser index; callbacks are not sent over HTTP. Define browser callbacks in a client module rather than passing functions across a Server Component boundary. Keep policy functions and synonym arrays stable to reuse the lazy index. Custom search controls can call useSearchContext() from the same public provider entry. Its search(query, namespace?, signal?) method returns Promise<SearchResult[]> .

records.text: The default config runs this plugin at priority -1.5 , after $RefPlugin ( -1 ) and before LazyPagePlugin ( -2 ), so titles and fields that come from $ref s are resolved.

records.title: SharedConfigPlugin
records.text: The SharedConfigPlugin crawls the page hierarchy to find the closest sharedConfig metadata from any parent index's page metadata. It then exports a JSON file into each directory with the merged config for that level. Shared config is typically the place where the following is configured for a Mosaic site: App Header configuration including site name and main navigation Footer information Help links for the left sidebar area

records.title: SharedConfigPlugin
records.text: Consider 2 sources the share the same namespace "product-docs": Source A - multiple product directories and main product index page. The index page specifies sharedConfig metadata. Source B - pages relevant to a single product. Index page does not have any sharedConfig metadata. Let's also assume that the pages from Source B would also naturally "fit" within the pages of Source B (e.g. inside a products directory). In this scenario, the SharedConfigPlugin will attempt to copy the shared config file from Source A into the root directory of Source B allowing the Source B pages to use the Source A sharedConfig as though it were a product sourced directly from Source A.

records.title: SidebarPlugin
records.text: The SidebarPlugin generates the necessary page metadata needed for the vertical navigation shown on some Mosaic pages. The output from the plugin is added to a sidebarData metadata property of the page.

records.title: SidebarPlugin
records.text: The rootDirGlob is used to determine the "root" directories of the sidebar. So for example: */*/* - generate sidebar data for the pages that are 3 directories deep in the filesystem hierarchy */!(product-a)/* - same as above but ignore the product-a directory products/product-b - generate a sidebar just for product-b in the products directory To rearrange pages in the sidebar or to apply a different label to a page you can configure the sidebar using page frontmatter. Set sidebar.exclude: true to hide a page's link without hiding its descendants. An excluded root or intermediate index.mdx still supplies the group's label, priority, and sort configuration. Empty groups are omitted, and a root whose pages are all excluded produces an empty sidebar. Previous/next navigation visits only included pages. For a namespace-wide tree, set rootDirGlob to that namespace's directory. Components can consume the generated tree through useSidebar().menu ; it does not need to be copied into sharedConfig.sidebar . Each root still needs a page directly within it to establish its structure.

records.title: SidebarPlugin
records.text: Import buildSidebarTree from @jpmorganchase/mosaic-plugins/sidebar to reuse Mosaic's traversal with your own storage and rendering. It accepts deserialized pages and returns the root group, without writing files or adding any sidebar or previous/next references. SidebarPlugin uses this same builder. The hooks receive newly created nodes. transformPage runs for visible pages; transformGroup runs bottom-up and receives the group's original index page, including an excluded index, or undefined when there is no index. Group priorities can therefore differ from Overview-page priorities. Add badges or other data in metadata . Input pages are not changed by the builder. compareNodes replaces sorting at every level and receives the parent group as a third argument. Use compareSidebarNodes first to preserve priority and configured field ordering, then add an alphabetical tie-break. Groups with no index retain their nested descendants. An empty non-root group is omitted. If no page sits directly within rootDir , the builder returns undefined . Call the builder from your own plugin module if you need these callbacks during content generation. Plugin configuration is sent to worker threads, so callbacks must live in the module rather than in serialized plugin options.
